description:
Solo R&D Toolmaker & Computational Engineer.

About Me: Ph.D. in Technological Sciences (KTH) specializing in computational modeling, multi-physics simulations, and physical metallurgy.

Project Scope: Building an interactive, SI-powered microgravity combustion dashboard for NASA’s Flame in Freefall challenge. Combining physics-informed models, transport phenomena analytics, and C/Python backends to process microgravity telemetry and evaluate fire safety thresholds for human spaceflight.
summary:
Fire safety in space is critical, as microgravity flames behave entirely differently due to the lack of buoyancy. This project provides an interactive, AI-powered dashboard analyzing real NASA SLICE and SPICE combustion experiments to support spacecraft fire safety.

The dashboard fulfills the challenge by providing an Experiment Explorer to visualize flame extinction events, a Comparative Analysis tool contrasting sooting vs. non-sooting flames, and an AI Safety Insights tab. For the AI, standard neural networks often "hallucinate" physically impossible values (like negative light) on sparse data. To solve this, I engineered a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) using PyTorch. By incorporating Fourier Feature Mapping and Bounded Energy Constraints, the model accurately tracks sharp extinction events while strictly obeying thermodynamic laws. This tool transforms complex microgravity data into actionable safety insights, demonstrating how physics-grounded AI can be used to protect future astronauts.
details:
What it does:
This dashboard ingests raw NASA telemetry and pixel intensity data from microgravity combustion experiments. It visualizes time-series data, correlates it with actual photographs of the flames, and uses a custom AI model to predict flame behavior.

How it works & Creativity:
The core innovation is a custom Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). Standard AI models suffer from "spectral bias" and often predict unphysical values (like negative light intensity) when extrapolating. I implemented Fourier Feature Mapping to allow the network to capture high-frequency events (like rapid flame extinction). Furthermore, I built a custom loss function enforcing bounded energy constraints—penalizing the AI if it predicts physically impossible values. This guarantees the AI adheres to the laws of thermodynamics.

Tools used:
Python, PyTorch (for the PINN architecture), Streamlit (for the web dashboard), Pandas/NumPy (data processing), and Plotly (interactive charts).

Benefits & Impact:
Understanding how fire behaves in microgravity is essential for the safety of future Artemis and Mars missions. This tool allows researchers to quickly interpret extinction limits (SLICE data) and smoke/soot production (SPICE data). It bridges the gap between raw NASA data and actionable engineering insights.
